silo_relevance: This paper is directly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it studies QAOA-based portfolio selection under tight qubit budgets and shows how encoding choices affect scalability, precision, and solution quality. Its main value for this silo is demonstrating that compressed asset encodings can preserve near-optimal portfolio rankings while using far fewer qubits than higher-resolution encodings.

key_points.point: Multi-stock-per-qubit encoding improves scalability with minimal loss in portfolio precision.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, this is the core result: it suggests more assets can be handled within limited quantum resources without materially degrading portfolio-selection quality.

key_points.point: Adding more qubits per stock yields negligible gains over the classical MVO baseline.
key_points.silo_note: This matters because it indicates diminishing returns from higher-resolution asset encodings, so extra qubits may not justify the added cost in portfolio selection workflows.

key_points.point: QAOA remains robust under aggressive compression, still finding the optimal or competitive portfolio ranking.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, robustness of the optimizer is crucial: even compressed encodings can still produce usable allocation decisions rather than only approximate feasibility.

key_points.point: The study’s main methodological contribution is a scalability-versus-precision comparison of encoding strategies for portfolio optimization.
key_points.silo_note: This is directly useful for portfolio_optimization because it frames the practical design tradeoff between qubit efficiency and portfolio solution quality.
